qa_pairs.question: What is the normal undergraduate credit load in Fall or Spring?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The normal undergraduate load is 12–18 credits in Fall or Spring.

contexts.text: Students register through the Northstar Portal during the dates published in `01_academic_calendar.md`. A student may register only when there is no active academic, conduct, advising, or financial hold. The normal undergraduate load is 12–18 credits in Fall or Spring and no more than 9 credits in Summer. Registration above 18 credits requires a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20 and written approval from the programme director.

qa_pairs.question: What is undergraduate tuition per registered credit for the 2026–2027 academic year?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Undergraduate tuition is USD 420 per registered credit for the 2026–2027 academic year.

contexts.text: Undergraduate tuition for the 2026–2027 academic year is USD 420 per registered credit. The student-services fee is USD 180 in Fall and Spring and USD 90 in Summer. Tuition and mandatory fees are due by the regular registration deadline listed in `01_academic_calendar.md`. A five-calendar-day grace period applies to the account balance, but it does not extend registration or scholarship deadlines.

qa_pairs.question: What percentage of undergraduate tuition does the Northstar Merit Scholarship cover?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The Northstar Merit Scholarship covers 50% of undergraduate tuition and does not cover student-services, late, or late-add fees.

contexts.text: The Northstar Merit Scholarship covers 50% of undergraduate tuition but does not cover student-services fees, late fees, or late-add fees. Initial awards are based on admission review. Renewal is assessed after each Fall and Spring term; Summer enrolment does not trigger a separate renewal review.

qa_pairs.question: What attendance percentage is normally expected in courses that record attendance?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance.

contexts.text: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A course syllabus may set a higher threshold when required by accreditation, laboratory safety, or clinical practice, but it may not set a lower threshold. Three consecutive unexplained absences trigger an academic-support alert; the alert itself is not a disciplinary finding.

qa_pairs.question: If a Fall 2026 student withdraws from one course on October 15 while remaining enrolled, how is it recorded and is it before the deadline?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: October 15 is after the September 4 census date but before the October 30 withdrawal deadline, so the course is recorded with a W. Stopping attendance alone would not count as withdrawal.

contexts.text: For Fall 2026, priority registration opens on July 20, regular registration closes on August 14, classes begin on August 17, and the standard add/drop period ends at 17:00 on August 28. Dropping one or more courses while remaining enrolled is a course withdrawal. Before or on census, the portal records a drop. After census and through the withdrawal deadline in `01_academic_calendar.md`, the course receives a `W`. After that deadline, withdrawal requires an exceptional-circumstances petition. Stopping attendance is not a withdrawal.

qa_pairs.question: Can a student with all academic graduation requirements completed receive degree conferral while a financial hold remains?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official degree conferral and release of the final transcript until the balance is resolved.

contexts.text: Degree conferral also requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved under `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`. A pending grade appeal may delay conferral if the disputed course affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold.

An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance. It does not remove a student from courses that were already confirmed. A payment plan is available for balances of at least USD 1,000; it requires 40% by the original due date and two equal monthly instalments. Missing an instalment creates a financial hold.

qa_pairs.question: A student believes a final grade contains a calculation error. What must the student do first, and what is the formal appeal deadline?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after publication. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and identify a permitted ground such as calculation error.

contexts.text: A disagreement about academic judgement is handled first with the instructor. Alleged calculation error, procedural unfairness, discrimination, or inconsistency with the published syllabus may proceed to the formal grade-appeal route in `08_student_support_and_appeals.md`.

A grade appeal is different from a service complaint. The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

contexts.text: Version 2.0 introduces a late-add window from the end of standard add/drop through the census date. qa_pairs.question: What are the main financial and scholarship consequences a student should check before withdrawing from every course?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A term withdrawal may affect tuition and scholarships. Ordinary withdrawal after census receives no tuition reversal; scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund. Scholarship pause or loss follows scholarship policy, so the student must review both policies before relying on a refund estimate.

contexts.text: Withdrawing from every course is a term withdrawal and may affect tuition, immigration status, housing, insurance, and scholarships. Tuition consequences are defined in `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`. Scholarship pause or loss is defined in `04_scholarships.md`. International students must consult the International Student Office before reducing their registered load.

For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal. Mandatory term fees are refundable only when the student withdraws from every course before classes begin.

An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. A voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the award; the student must request a scholarship deferral before the census date. Scholarship decisions may be appealed within ten business days using the process in `08_student_support_and_appeals.md`.

qa_pairs.question: What should a student do after suspecting that their portal account has been compromised, and what sensitive information must not be put in the ticket?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student should change the password from a trusted device, revoke active sessions, and contact the IT Service Desk. The ticket may include the case number and event time but must not include passwords, authentication codes, full card numbers, or unrelated personal records.

contexts.text: Northstar uses the student portal and university email for official account communication. Multi-factor authentication is required for the portal. Staff will never request a password or one-time authentication code. A student who suspects account compromise should change the password from a trusted device, revoke active sessions, and contact the IT Service Desk. Suspected payment fraud should also be reported to Student Accounts and the student's payment provider.

Security incidents involving immediate unauthorized disclosure are escalated to the Privacy Officer. Routine access questions go first to the IT Service Desk. Students should include a case number and event time, but should not copy passwords, authentication codes, full card numbers, or unrelated personal records into a ticket.

qa_pairs.question: A Merit Scholarship student failed one academic renewal requirement, then takes an approved medical leave. What happens to the award and probation opportunity?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A first academic renewal failure normally results in one term of scholarship probation while the award remains active. An approved medical leave can then pause the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. The leave still requires the applicable approval process.

contexts.text: A first failure to meet one academic renewal requirement normally produces one term of scholarship probation rather than immediate loss. During probation, the award remains active. A second consecutive failed review ends the award beginning with the next term. A serious-conduct sanction may end the award immediately and is not protected by the academic probation rule.

An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. A voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the award; the student must request a scholarship deferral before the census date. Scholarship decisions may be appealed within ten business days using the process in `08_student_support_and_appeals.md`.

A leave of absence pauses active enrolment while preserving the student's programme place. A standard leave may last one or two consecutive regular terms. The student must submit the request before the census date, explain the reason, provide any required documentation, and obtain programme approval. Employment, travel, family responsibilities, and health circumstances may support a request, but approval is not automatic.

contexts.text: An `I` incomplete grade may be granted when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently. The student and instructor must sign an incomplete plan. The default deadline is the end of the next regular term. If no grade is submitted by that deadline, the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists.

qa_pairs.question: A documented medical condition prevented timely withdrawal and filing. What timing rule applies to retroactive medical leave, and what kind of tuition relief may follow?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A retroactive medical-leave request normally must be filed within 30 calendar days after the last documented participation. A later request needs evidence that the condition also prevented filing during those 30 days. If medical withdrawal is approved, the student may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study based on the last documented participation date; it is not a cash refund, and scholarship funds are adjusted first.

contexts.text: Medical leave may be approved retroactively when a documented condition prevented timely submission. A retroactive request must normally be filed within 30 calendar days after the student's last documented participation. Later requests require evidence that the condition also prevented filing during that 30-day period. Medical documentation should describe functional impact and relevant dates; it should not be emailed to individual instructors.

An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund and requires the process in `06_leave_and_withdrawal.md`. Scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated. Students with scholarships must therefore review `04_scholarships.md`; a refund estimate shown before scholarship adjustment is not final.

qa_pairs.question: A student has completed 120 applicable credits and meets the GPA requirement but has a financial hold and a pending appeal in a required course. Can the degree be conferred or proved by attending commencement?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. Academic eligibility also requires all programme courses and the capstone, while official conferral requires all holds cleared. A pending appeal may delay conferral if it affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold. Commencement participation is only ceremonial and does not prove conferral.

contexts.text: An undergraduate student is academically eligible to graduate after completing at least 120 applicable credits, all programme-required courses, the capstone requirement, and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00. At least 30 of the final 45 applicable credits must be completed at Northstar University unless an approved exchange agreement states otherwise.

Degree conferral also requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved under `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`. A pending grade appeal may delay conferral if the disputed course affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold.

Participation in a commencement ceremony is ceremonial and is not proof that a degree has been conferred. Students with no more than six credits remaining may request permission to participate early, but the transcript will not show the degree until every requirement and hold is cleared.
